goryeo.notes: All checked: 918 founding/936 unification, Wang Geon marriage alliances and northern expansion policy (Goguryeo succession); Gwangjong slave review act + first gwageo (958); Seongjong adopted Choe Seung-ro's 28-article memorial; Seo Hui 1st Khitan invasion (993) Gangdong 6 ju; Gang Gam-chan 3rd invasion Gwiju (1019); military coup 1170 (late 12th c.); Ganghwa capital move against Mongols; Sambyeolcho formed under military regime, Ganghwa->Jindo->Jeju, resisted until 1273; Gongmin attacked Ssangseong commandery to recover land north of Cheollyeong, employed Sin Don; Tripitaka Koreana carved during Mongol invasions, kept at Haeinsa Janggyeong Panjeon; Jikji printed in late Goryeo (1377) with metal type, oldest extant, in Bibliotheque nationale de France; inlaid celadon description correct. '약 500년' (474 yrs) acceptable approximation. Compare row order (truce -> Sambyeolcho to 1273 -> Yuan interference) matches standard textbook presentation. No exam-frequency or statistics claims.

colonial.notes: All checked: 1910-1945 scope; 1910s gendarme-police rule and land survey project; March 1 Movement 1919 -> Provisional Government in Shanghai same year, and change to 'cultural rule'; Bongodong (Jun 1920, Hong Beom-do's Korean Independence Army) and Cheongsanri (Oct 1920, Kim Jwa-jin's Northern Military Administration with Hong's units); Korean Patriotic Organization founded by Kim Gu in Shanghai, Lee Bong-chang bomb at Japanese emperor, Yun Bong-gil Hongkou Park 1932 (generals/officials killed or injured); Korean Liberation Army 1940 Chongqing; June 10 Movement 1926, Gwangju Student Movement 1929 (described as largest since March 1st, the standard textbook characterization); late-1930s assimilation policies (Korean language suppression, name change); Korean Language Society 1933 unified orthography and dictionary work; Joseon studies movement c.1934 with Jeong In-bo; 1942 Korean Language Society incident and dissolution. Para 3 lists 1926/1929 after 1940 but explicitly separated as domestic events with years, so not misleading. No exam-frequency or statistics claims.
